section: Bayt Al Ghaf in one paragraph
text:
## Bayt Al Ghaf in one paragraph

Bayt Al Ghaf is a contemporary Emirati restaurant and majlis in the Al Seef heritage quarter on the Bur Dubai side of Dubai Creek. The kitchen cooks the dishes Emirati families eat at home — machboos, harees, thareed, saloona and luqaimat — with careful sourcing, house-ground bezar and slow, unhurried cooking, and serves them in a dining room of coral-stone walls, palm-frond ceilings and creek views.

Bayt Al Ghaf (Arabic: بيت الغاف) describes itself as “Emirati kitchen & majlis on Dubai Creek”. It opened in 2019. Cuisine: Emirati, Gulf (Khaleeji) and Contemporary Emirati.

section: What the name Bayt Al Ghaf means
text:
## What the name Bayt Al Ghaf means

Bayt Al Ghaf means “House of the Ghaf” — the ghaf (Prosopis cineraria) is the UAE's national tree, a symbol of shade, endurance and hospitality in the desert. The restaurant's sign is a brass ghaf tree on a coral-stone building.

section: The story of Bayt Al Ghaf
text:
## The story of Bayt Al Ghaf

Bayt Al Ghaf began with a family majlis in Al Bastakiya and a ghaf tree in the courtyard, where neighbours gathered for gahwa, dates and long conversations.

Chef Hessa grew up a few streets from the creek, in a house where machboos was cooked every Friday and harees simmered all night before Eid. Bayt Al Ghaf brings that kitchen to Al Seef: the same unhurried methods, the same respect for rice, lamb, dates and loomi, served in a coral-stone dining room that looks out over the abras.

text:
## Chef Hessa, head chef of Bayt Al Ghaf

Chef Hessa is the head chef of Bayt Al Ghaf. She grew up in Al Bastakiya, a few streets from Dubai Creek and a few minutes' walk from the restaurant. Her family cooked machboos every Friday and harees overnight before Eid, and the Bayt Al Ghaf menu is built on those home recipes, alongside a few contemporary dishes that use local camel, dates and loomi.

section: How the Bayt Al Ghaf kitchen cooks
text:
## How the Bayt Al Ghaf kitchen cooks

- The bezar spice blend is toasted and ground in-house every week.
- Regag bread is stretched on the hot iron plate in front of guests, and chebab is baked to order.
- Seafood comes from licensed Gulf suppliers; hammour is bought only outside the seasonal fishing ban.
- Harees is cooked overnight in one batch, so it is limited each day.
- All meat and poultry are halal, and the restaurant is alcohol-free.
- Contemporary dishes include camel kofta with the walnut-and-pepper Al Ghaf House Red sauce, a camel burger glazed with Sauce No. 7, and ice cream churned from UAE camel milk and dates.

section: Bayt Al Ghaf dining rooms and seats
text:
## Bayt Al Ghaf dining rooms and seats

Bayt Al Ghaf has 154 seats: 88 indoors (the main dining hall and the creek-view window tables), 36 on the seasonal creek terrace and 30 in two private majlis rooms with traditional floor seating (Majlis Al Sidr and Majlis Al Ghaf). The dining room has coral-stone walls, palm-frond ceilings and views over the abras and dhows on the creek.

section: Bayt Al Ghaf signature dishes
text:
## Bayt Al Ghaf signature dishes

- Balaleet (بلاليط), AED 34: Sweet saffron and cardamom vermicelli crowned with a thin omelette.
- Harees (هريس), AED 48: Wheat and lamb slow-cooked overnight and beaten smooth, finished with ghee.
- Lamb Thareed (ثريد لحم), AED 62: Lamb and vegetable saloona ladled over layers of regag bread.
- Lamb Machboos (مجبوس لحم), AED 72: Our signature: bone-in lamb shoulder and spiced basmati with loomi and hashu.
- Muhammar with Fried Safi (محمر وصافي), AED 69: Sweet saffron and date-syrup rice with a whole fried rabbitfish.
- Luqaimat (لقيمات), AED 32: Crisp saffron-cardamom dumplings, warm dibs and toasted sesame.
- Gahwa Emirati (Dallah for the Table) (قهوة عربية), AED 30: A dallah of lightly roasted Arabic coffee with cardamom and saffron, served with dates.
- Karak Chai (شاي كرك), AED 12: Strong black tea simmered with evaporated milk, cardamom and saffron.
- Friday Family Machboos Platter (صينية مجبوس الجمعة), AED 349: Fridays only. Serves 5: lamb shoulder and whole chicken machboos on one great tray.
- Whole Lamb Ouzi (أوزي), AED 1,450: Catering only. Serves 10–12: whole slow-roasted lamb on spiced rice with nuts.

section: Bayt Al Ghaf values: welcome, generosity and respect
text:
## Bayt Al Ghaf values: welcome, generosity and respect

- Welcome (الترحيب): every table is welcomed with gahwa from the dallah and Khalas dates. Coffee is poured from right to left; a gentle shake of the finjan says you have had enough.
- Generosity (الكرم): Emirati meals are shared. Platters and machboos are portioned generously, and family-style serving is always offered.
- Respect (الاحترام): a family restaurant — alcohol-free, smoke-free and modest. Children are welcome, and the majlis rooms give families privacy.

section: Bayt Al Ghaf hours on holidays and special days
text:
## Bayt Al Ghaf hours on holidays and special days

- Winter season 2026–27 (2026-11-01 to 2027-02-28): Winter dessert menu (Aseedat Bobar) is served during this period.
- Eid Al Etihad (UAE National Day) 2026 (2026-12-01 to 2026-12-03): Eid Al Etihad Feast available. Normal opening hours. Pre-orders for the feast open on 15 November 2026.
- Ramadan 2027 (provisional) (2027-02-08 to 2027-03-09, provisional — subject to moon sighting): open 12:00 (noon) to midnight (24:00) every day. Provisional dates subject to moon sighting. During Ramadan we open from 12:00 to 24:00 daily, breakfast is not served, and the Iftar Set Menu is available from sunset.
- Eid Al Fitr 2027 (provisional) (2027-03-10 to 2027-03-12, provisional — subject to moon sighting): Provisional dates. The restaurant opens at 14:00 on the first day of Eid and keeps normal hours on the following days.
- 2026-11-14: The dining room is closed to the public from 18:00 on Saturday 14 November 2026 for a private event. Takeaway and delivery continue as normal.
- 2027-03-10: On the first day of Eid Al Fitr (provisionally 10 March 2027) we open at 14:00.
- On other public holidays the restaurant keeps its normal hours unless a closure is announced.

section: Can Bayt Al Ghaf stay open late for a group?
text:
## Can Bayt Al Ghaf stay open late for a group?

No. Bayt Al Ghaf cannot extend its opening hours for individual guests or groups. For a late private event, the events team (events@baytalghaf.example) can discuss a private booking in advance, but nothing beyond the published hours can be promised by phone.

section: Facilities at Bayt Al Ghaf
text:
## Facilities at Bayt Al Ghaf

- Indoor dining hall with creek-view window tables
- Outdoor creek terrace (seasonal, mid-October to end of April)
- Two private majlis rooms with traditional floor seating
- Step-free entrance from the Al Seef promenade and an accessible restroom
- Six high chairs and a baby-changing table in the accessible restroom
- Free Wi-Fi (network “BaytAlGhaf-Guest”, password printed on the menu)
- Prayer room for men and women on the first floor of the Heritage Quarter building (shared facility)
- Takeaway collection counter at the Al Seef Street entrance
- Live oud music on Friday evenings, 20:00–22:00

section: The Bayt Al Ghaf menu in brief
text:
## The Bayt Al Ghaf menu in brief

Bayt Al Ghaf serves Emirati home cooking: machboos, harees, thareed, saloona, regag, luqaimat, Gulf seafood, charcoal grills and contemporary camel dishes. The menu has 46 dishes in 11 sections. Prices run from AED 10 (Sulaimani) to AED 355 (Eid Al Etihad Feast (National Day)) for regular dishes; catering items such as the Whole Lamb Ouzi cost more.

All prices are in UAE dirhams (AED) and include 5% VAT. All meat and poultry are halal. Bayt Al Ghaf is alcohol-free and uses no pork or gelatine.

section: How allergens are listed on the Bayt Al Ghaf menu
text:
## How allergens are listed on the Bayt Al Ghaf menu

Every Bayt Al Ghaf dish lists the allergens it contains as ingredients and the allergens it may contain as traces. Allergen information is worked out from each ingredient, including the ingredients inside sauces, marinades and spice blends, so a dish's allergens always match its recipe. Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

section: How Bayt Al Ghaf rates spice
text:
## How Bayt Al Ghaf rates spice

Bayt Al Ghaf rates each dish from 0 to 3: 0 = not spicy, 1 = mild (warm spices such as bezar rather than chilli heat), 2 = medium-hot, 3 = hot. Emirati food is generally fragrant rather than fiery; most heat comes from dakkus, the tomato-chilli sauce served on the side.

Bezar Spice Blend (بزار) is a spice blend. The Emirati house spice blend that seasons our machboos, saloona and grills. Whole spices are toasted and ground in-house every week. Bezar Spice Blend is served with Bayd w Tamat, Weekend Fuala Breakfast Spread, Sambousa Trio, Hummus with Spiced Lamb & Pine Nuts, Lamb Thareed, Saloonat Dajaj, Saloonat Samak (Monday), Margooga Laham (Tuesday), Madrooba Dajaj (Wednesday), Lamb Machboos, Chicken Machboos, Camel Machboos (Thursday), Camel Kofta, Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli, Vegetable Machboos, Bamia Saloona, Pumpkin & Chickpea Saloona, Majlis Sharing Platter, Friday Family Machboos Platter, Whole Lamb Ouzi, Office Machboos Lunch Box, Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person) and Eid Al Etihad Feast (National Day). Bezar Spice Blend is part of Hashu Topping, Sauce No. 7 (Saba'a), Bezar & Lime Fish Marinade and Laban Marinade.

section: What Balaleet is
text:
## What Balaleet is

The classic Emirati breakfast of sweet and savoury: fine wheat vermicelli toasted in ghee, steamed with saffron, cardamom, rosewater and sugar, and topped with a thin, lightly salted omelette.

How Balaleet is cooked: Vermicelli toasted in ghee then steamed; omelette cooked on the plancha. Style: Traditional Emirati breakfast, cooked to order.

Guests also ask for Balaleet as “balalit”, “balaleet”, “sweet vermicelli”, “vermicelli with egg” or “vermicelli omelette”. These are common spellings and descriptions of the same dish.

section: Balaleet: allergens
text:
## Balaleet: allergens

Balaleet contains gluten (wheat), eggs and milk (dairy) as ingredients in its standard recipe. Where each allergen comes from:

- Gluten (wheat): from the wheat vermicelli
- Eggs: from the eggs
- Milk (dairy): from the ghee

Balaleet has no specific trace warnings beyond the general kitchen statement below.

Balaleet contains no crustaceans (prawns and shrimp), molluscs, fish, peanuts, soy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites or lupin.

Kitchen allergen statement: Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

section: Questions guests ask about Balaleet
text:
## Questions guests ask about Balaleet

**Q: Is balaleet sweet or savoury?**

A: Both: the vermicelli is sweet with saffron, cardamom and rosewater, and the thin omelette on top is lightly salted.

**Q: Can I have it without egg?**

A: Yes — choose “No omelette”. The vermicelli itself has no egg, but it is cooked on the same plancha as egg dishes.

**Q: Is it vegetarian?**

A: Yes, it is vegetarian. It contains wheat (gluten), milk (ghee) and eggs, so it is not vegan.

**Q: How much is Balaleet?**

A: Balaleet costs AED 34 (34 dirhams), including VAT.

**Q: How many people does Balaleet serve?**

A: Balaleet serves one person (about 280 g — 200 g of vermicelli with a two-egg omelette).

**Q: Is Balaleet vegan?**

A: Balaleet is not vegan; it is vegetarian (contains dairy, eggs or honey, but no meat or fish).

**Q: Does Balaleet contain nuts?**

A: Balaleet has no nut ingredients. The kitchen is not nut-free.

**Q: Does Balaleet contain dairy?**

A: Yes, Balaleet contains milk (dairy).

**Q: Is Balaleet gluten-free?**

A: No, Balaleet contains gluten (wheat).

**Q: How spicy is Balaleet?**

A: Balaleet is not spicy (spice level 0 of 3). Not spicy. Sweetness can be reduced (choose “Less sweet”).

**Q: Can I get Balaleet delivered?**

A: No, Balaleet is not delivered. It can be ordered for dine-in, pickup (takeaway) or dine-in pre-order.

**Q: How long does Balaleet take?**

A: Balaleet takes about 12 minutes to prepare. For a pickup order, allow at least 22 minutes from ordering.

**Q: When can I order Balaleet?**

A: Balaleet is on the menu every day of the week. Balaleet is served from 08:00 (8 am) until 11:30 (11:30 am). Balaleet is part of the Emirati breakfast menu, served 08:00 (8 am) to 11:30 (11:30 am).

**Q: Does Balaleet contain dairy?**

**Q: Can I get Balaleet delivered?**

A: No, Balaleet is not delivered. It can be ordered for dine-in, pickup (takeaway) or dine-in pre-order.

A: Balaleet is on the menu every day of the week. Balaleet is served from 08:00 (8 am) until 11:30 (11:30 am). Balaleet is part of the Emirati breakfast menu, served 08:00 (8 am) to 11:30 (11:30 am).

## Chebab with Date Syrup & Cream Cheese: allergens

Chebab with Date Syrup & Cream Cheese contains gluten (wheat), eggs and milk (dairy) as ingredients in its standard recipe. Where each allergen comes from:

- Gluten (wheat): from the wheat flour
- Eggs: from the eggs
- Milk (dairy): from the full-cream milk, the ghee and the cream cheese

Chebab with Date Syrup & Cream Cheese has no specific trace warnings beyond the general kitchen statement below.

Chebab with Date Syrup & Cream Cheese contains no crustaceans (prawns and shrimp), molluscs, fish, peanuts, soy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites or lupin.

Kitchen allergen statement: Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

section: Regag with Egg & Cheese: allergens
text:
## Regag with Egg & Cheese: allergens

Regag with Egg & Cheese contains gluten (wheat), eggs and milk (dairy) as ingredients in its standard recipe. Where each allergen comes from:

- Gluten (wheat): from the regag bread
- Eggs: from the eggs
- Milk (dairy): from the processed cheese and the ghee

Regag with Egg & Cheese has no specific trace warnings beyond the general kitchen statement below.

Regag with Egg & Cheese contains no crustaceans (prawns and shrimp), molluscs, fish, peanuts, soy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites or lupin.

Kitchen allergen statement: Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

section: What Sambousa Trio is
text:
## What Sambousa Trio is

Hand-folded triangles of thin pastry, fried until crisp: two filled with bezar-spiced minced lamb and onion, two with akkawi cheese and coriander, and two with potato, carrot and green chilli. Served with dakkus for dipping.

How Sambousa Trio is cooked: Deep-fried in sunflower oil. Style: Gulf street snack, a Ramadan staple.

Guests also ask for Sambousa Trio as “sambousa”, “samosa”, “sambusa” or “samboosa”. These are common spellings and descriptions of the same dish.

## Sambousa Trio: sauces, marinades and spice blends

**Bezar Spice Blend** (بزار) is cooked into Sambousa Trio (seasons the lamb filling). The Emirati house spice blend that seasons our machboos, saloona and grills. Whole spices are toasted and ground in-house every week. Bezar Spice Blend is made from coriander seed, cumin, fennel seed, black pepper, turmeric, cinnamon, green cardamom, dried red chilli, cloves and nutmeg. Bezar Spice Blend contains none of the 14 major allergens and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

**Dakkus Tomato-Chilli Sauce** (دقوس) is served on the side with Sambousa Trio. The Gulf's classic tomato and chilli sauce, served on the side of every machboos so guests can add heat to taste. Dakkus Tomato-Chilli Sauce is made from tomato, tomato paste, garlic, green chilli, dried red chilli, lime, cumin, sunflower oil and salt. section: Sambousa Trio: allergens
text:
## Sambousa Trio: allergens

Sambousa Trio contains gluten (wheat) and milk (dairy) as ingredients in its standard recipe. Where each allergen comes from:

- Gluten (wheat): from the sambousa pastry sheets
- Milk (dairy): from the white brined cheese

Sambousa Trio may contain traces of eggs, celery, mustard and sesame. Reasons:

- Fried in the general fryer, which is shared with sambousa, luqaimat, khanfaroosh and potato wedges (wheat, milk, eggs and sesame).
- Ground spices are packed by a supplier that also handles mustard and celery.

Sambousa Trio contains no crustaceans (prawns and shrimp), molluscs, fish, peanuts, soy, tree nuts, sulphites or lupin.

Kitchen allergen statement: Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

section: What Nakhi is
text:
## What Nakhi is

Chickpeas simmered until soft, then tossed with toasted cumin, a pinch of dried chilli, sea salt, lime and fresh coriander. A humble, much-loved snack sold by Emirati street vendors for generations.

How Nakhi is cooked: Boiled and tossed warm. Style: Traditional Emirati snack.

Guests also ask for Nakhi as “nakhi”, “dango”, “chickpeas”, “spiced chickpeas” or “nikhi”. These are common spellings and descriptions of the same dish.

Nakhi may contain traces of celery and mustard. Reasons:

Nakhi contains no gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns and shrimp), molluscs, eggs, fish, peanuts, soy, milk (dairy), tree nuts, sesame, sulphites or lupin.

Kitchen allergen statement: Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

## Hummus with Spiced Lamb & Pine Nuts: allergens

Hummus with Spiced Lamb & Pine Nuts contains gluten (wheat), tree nuts and sesame as ingredients in its standard recipe. Where each allergen comes from:

- Gluten (wheat): from the regag bread
- Tree nuts: from the pine nuts
- Sesame: from the tahini

Hummus with Spiced Lamb & Pine Nuts may contain traces of celery and mustard. Reasons:

- Ground spices are packed by a supplier that also handles mustard and celery.

Hummus with Spiced Lamb & Pine Nuts contains no crustaceans (prawns and shrimp), molluscs, eggs, fish, peanuts, soy, milk (dairy), sulphites or lupin.

Kitchen allergen statement: Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

section: Mehyawa Regag Bites: allergens
text:
## Mehyawa Regag Bites: allergens

Mehyawa Regag Bites contains gluten (wheat), eggs, fish, milk (dairy) and mustard as ingredients in its standard recipe. Where each allergen comes from:

- Gluten (wheat): from the regag bread
- Eggs: from the eggs
- Fish: from the Mehyawa, which contains small salted fish
- Milk (dairy): from the processed cheese
- Mustard: from the Mehyawa, which contains mustard seeds

Mehyawa Regag Bites may contain traces of celery. Reasons:

- Ground spices are packed by a supplier that also handles mustard and celery.

Mehyawa Regag Bites contains no crustaceans (prawns and shrimp), molluscs, peanuts, soy, tree nuts, sesame, sulphites or lupin.

Kitchen allergen statement: Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

**Q: What is mehyawa?**

A: Mehyawa is a traditional Gulf fermented fish sauce made from small salted fish with mustard seed, cumin, fennel and coriander. It contains fish and mustard.

**Q: I can't eat fish — can you leave out the mehyawa?**

A: No, mehyawa is the point of this dish. Order Regag with Egg & Cheese from the breakfast menu instead (before 11:30).

**Q: How much is Mehyawa Regag Bites?**

**Q: How many people does Mehyawa Regag Bites serve?**

A: Mehyawa Regag Bites serves 2 people (8 bites from 2 regag (about 150 g)).

**Q: Is Mehyawa Regag Bites vegan?**

A: Mehyawa Regag Bites is not vegan; it is pescatarian (contains fish or seafood, no meat).

**Q: Does Mehyawa Regag Bites contain dairy?**

A: No, Mehyawa Regag Bites contains gluten (wheat).

**Q: How spicy is Mehyawa Regag Bites?**

A: Mehyawa Regag Bites is mild (spice level 1 of 3). Mehyawa is savoury and pungent rather than hot; it cannot be removed from this dish.

**Q: Can I get Mehyawa Regag Bites delivered?**

A: No, Mehyawa Regag Bites is not delivered. It can be ordered for dine-in, pickup (takeaway) or dine-in pre-order.

**Q: How long does Mehyawa Regag Bites take?**

A: Mehyawa Regag Bites takes about 8 minutes to prepare. For a pickup order, allow at least 20 minutes from ordering.

A: Mehyawa Regag Bites is on the menu every day of the week. Mehyawa Regag Bites is served all day, from opening at 08:00 (8 am) until the kitchen's last orders 30 minutes before closing. A single regular order can include up to 10 Mehyawa Regag Bites.

section: What Harees is
text:
## What Harees is

One of the oldest Emirati dishes: whole hulled wheat and lamb cooked slowly overnight in a sealed pot, then beaten with a wooden madhrab until smooth and elastic. Served with a pool of warm ghee and a dusting of cinnamon. Made in a single batch each night, so quantities are limited.

How Harees is cooked: Slow-cooked for 10 hours, then beaten by hand. Style: Traditional Emirati festive and Ramadan dish.

Guests also ask for Harees as “harees”, “harris”, “hareis”, “haris” or “wheat and meat porridge”. These are common spellings and descriptions of the same dish.

- Gluten (wheat): from the hulled wheat
- Milk (dairy): from the ghee

Harees contains no crustaceans (prawns and shrimp), molluscs, eggs, fish, peanuts, soy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites or lupin.

Kitchen allergen statement: Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

section: Questions guests ask about Lamb Thareed
text:
## Questions guests ask about Lamb Thareed

**Q: What is the difference between thareed and saloona?**

A: Saloona is the stew served with rice; thareed is a saloona poured over regag bread so the bread soaks up the broth.

**Q: Can thareed be gluten-free?**

A: No — the regag bread is an essential part of thareed. For a gluten-free-ingredient alternative, try Saloonat Dajaj with rice.

**Q: How much is Lamb Thareed?**

A: Lamb Thareed costs AED 62 (62 dirhams), including VAT.

**Q: How many people does Lamb Thareed serve?**

A: Lamb Thareed serves one person (about 550 g: 200 g bone-in lamb, vegetables and 80 g regag).

**Q: Is Lamb Thareed vegan?**

A: Lamb Thareed is not vegan; it is a meat dish (contains halal meat or poultry).

**Q: Does Lamb Thareed contain nuts?**

A: Lamb Thareed has no nut ingredients. The kitchen is not nut-free.

**Q: Does Lamb Thareed contain dairy?**

A: Yes, Lamb Thareed contains milk (dairy).

**Q: Is Lamb Thareed gluten-free?**

A: No, Lamb Thareed contains gluten (wheat).

**Q: How spicy is Lamb Thareed?**

A: Lamb Thareed is mild (spice level 1 of 3). The chilli in the saloona can be reduced; extra dakkus can be added for heat.

**Q: Can I get Lamb Thareed delivered?**

A: Yes, Lamb Thareed can be delivered within Bayt Al Ghaf's delivery zones, 12:00 (noon) to 22:30 (10:30 pm).

**Q: How long does Lamb Thareed take?**

A: Lamb Thareed takes about 15 minutes to prepare. For a pickup order, allow at least 25 minutes from ordering.

**Q: When can I order Lamb Thareed?**

A: Lamb Thareed is on the menu every day of the week. Lamb Thareed is served from 12:00 (noon) until the kitchen closes. A single regular order can include up to 10 Lamb Thareed.

## What Saloonat Samak (Monday) is

Every Monday, our kingfish (kanaad) steaks are marinated in bezar and lime, then simmered in a tangy tamarind and tomato saloona with loomi, garlic and green chilli. Served with white basmati rice and fresh coriander.

How Saloonat Samak (Monday) is cooked: Marinated, then simmered in sauce. Style: Coastal Emirati fish stew.

Guests also ask for Saloonat Samak (Monday) as “fish saloona”, “fish stew”, “fish curry”, “kingfish stew” or “kanaad saloona”. These are common spellings and descriptions of the same dish.

section: What Margooga Laham (Tuesday) is
text:
## What Margooga Laham (Tuesday) is

A hearty winter-in-the-desert dish: lamb, eggplant, potato and tomato simmered with loomi and bezar, then hand-stretched sheets of dough are laid into the pot to cook in the broth until silky.

How Margooga Laham (Tuesday) is cooked: Braised, then finished with dough sheets. Style: Traditional Emirati stew.

Guests also ask for Margooga Laham (Tuesday) as “margooga”, “marqooqa”, “margoogat”, “marqouq” or “lamb stew with dough”. These are common spellings and descriptions of the same dish.

- Ground spices are packed by a supplier that also handles mustard and celery.

We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

section: What Lamb Machboos is
text:
## What Lamb Machboos is

The national dish of the Emirates, cooked our way: bone-in lamb shoulder braised until tender with onion, tomato, ginger, garlic and whole loomi, then basmati rice is cooked in the same spiced stock with bezar, cinnamon, cardamom and cloves. Crowned with hashu (caramelised onions and golden raisins) and served with dakkus.

How Lamb Machboos is cooked: Lamb braised for 2.5 hours; rice steamed in the braising stock. Style: Traditional Emirati machboos.

Guests also ask for Lamb Machboos as “machboos”, “majboos”, “machbous”, “makbous”, “kabsa”, “lamb rice”, “rice with lamb” or “lamb kabsa”. These are common spellings and descriptions of the same dish.

Crowned with hashu (caramelised onions and golden raisins) and served with dakkus.

How Lamb Machboos is cooked: Lamb braised for 2.5 hours; rice steamed in the braising stock. Style: Traditional Emirati machboos.

Guests also ask for Lamb Machboos as “machboos”, “majboos”, “machbous”, “makbous”, “kabsa”, “lamb rice”, “rice with lamb” or “lamb kabsa”. These are common spellings and descriptions of the same dish.

## Lamb Machboos: sauces, marinades and spice blends

**Bezar Spice Blend** (بزار) is cooked into Lamb Machboos (5 g). The Emirati house spice blend that seasons our machboos, saloona and grills. Whole spices are toasted and ground in-house every week. Bezar Spice Blend is made from coriander seed, cumin, fennel seed, black pepper, turmeric, cinnamon, green cardamom, dried red chilli, cloves and nutmeg. Bezar Spice Blend contains none of the 14 major allergens and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

**Hashu Topping** (حشو) is spooned on top of Lamb Machboos (35 g). Slow-caramelised onions with golden raisins, ghee and a little bezar — the sweet-savoury crown of a traditional machboos. Hashu Topping is made from onion, golden raisins, ghee (clarified butter), sugar, green cardamom, salt and Bezar Spice Blend. Hashu Topping contains milk (dairy) and sulphites and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

**Dakkus Tomato-Chilli Sauce** (دقوس) is served on the side with Lamb Machboos (50 ml). The Gulf's classic tomato and chilli sauce, served on the side of every machboos so guests can add heat to taste. Dakkus Tomato-Chilli Sauce is made from tomato, tomato paste, garlic, green chilli, dried red chilli, lime, cumin, sunflower oil and salt. Dakkus Tomato-Chilli Sauce contains none of the 14 major allergens and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

section: Lamb Machboos: allergens
text:
## Lamb Machboos: allergens

Lamb Machboos contains milk (dairy) and sulphites as ingredients in its standard recipe. Where each allergen comes from:

- Milk (dairy): from the ghee and the Hashu Topping, which contains ghee
- Sulphites: from the Hashu Topping, which contains golden raisins

Lamb Machboos may contain traces of celery and mustard. Reasons:

- Ground spices are packed by a supplier that also handles mustard and celery.

Lamb Machboos contains no gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns and shrimp), molluscs, eggs, fish, peanuts, soy, tree nuts, sesame or lupin.

Kitchen allergen statement: Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

section: Lamb Machboos: how spicy it is
text:
## Lamb Machboos: how spicy it is

Lamb Machboos is mild (spice level 1 of 3) as standard. Machboos is mild (warm spice rather than chilli heat) and cannot be made milder: the rice is cooked in stock seasoned with bezar. The heat comes from the dakkus served on the side, which can be skipped or doubled.

Can the spice be reduced? No. Can it be made spicier? Yes.

text:
## Questions guests ask about Lamb Machboos (part 1 of 2)

A: Machboos is the Emirati national rice dish: meat (here, lamb) and basmati rice cooked together in stock spiced with bezar and dried black lime (loomi).

**Q: Is the lamb on the bone?**

A: Yes, it is a bone-in piece of lamb shoulder — about 280 g raw, roughly 180 g cooked.

**Q: Can I have it without raisins?**

A: Yes. Choose “Hashu without raisins” or “No hashu”. Note that the raisins are the only source of sulphites in this dish.

**Q: Does lamb machboos contain nuts?**

A: No nut ingredients are used in lamb machboos. Our kitchen does handle nuts, so we cannot guarantee it is free from traces.

**Q: Is it spicy?**

A: It is mild — warm spice rather than chilli heat. Dakkus on the side adds heat if you want it.

**Q: How much is Lamb Machboos?**

A: Lamb Machboos costs AED 72 (72 dirhams), including VAT.

**Q: How many people does Lamb Machboos serve?**

A: Lamb Machboos serves one person (about 650 g: 280 g bone-in lamb (raw weight, about 180 g cooked) and 150 g (dry) basmati rice).

**Q: Is Lamb Machboos vegan?**

A: Lamb Machboos is not vegan; it is a meat dish (contains halal meat or poultry).

**Q: Does Lamb Machboos contain nuts?**

A: Lamb Machboos has no nut ingredients. The kitchen is not nut-free.

**Q: Does Lamb Machboos contain dairy?**

A: Yes, Lamb Machboos contains milk (dairy).

**Q: Is Lamb Machboos gluten-free?**

A: Lamb Machboos has no gluten-containing ingredients, but Bayt Al Ghaf is not a certified gluten-free kitchen.

**Q: How spicy is Lamb Machboos?**

A: Lamb Machboos is mild (spice level 1 of 3). Machboos is mild (warm spice rather than chilli heat) and cannot be made milder: the rice is cooked in stock seasoned with bezar. The heat comes from the dakkus served on the side, which can be skipped or doubled.

**Q: Can I get Lamb Machboos delivered?**

A: Yes, Lamb Machboos can be delivered within Bayt Al Ghaf's delivery zones, 12:00 (noon) to 22:30 (10:30 pm).

**Q: How long does Lamb Machboos take?**

A: Lamb Machboos takes about 15 minutes to prepare. For a pickup order, allow at least 25 minutes from ordering.

**Q: When can I order Lamb Machboos?**

## Chicken Machboos: sauces, marinades and spice blends

**Bezar Spice Blend** (بزار) is cooked into Chicken Machboos (5 g). The Emirati house spice blend that seasons our machboos, saloona and grills. Whole spices are toasted and ground in-house every week. Bezar Spice Blend is made from coriander seed, cumin, fennel seed, black pepper, turmeric, cinnamon, green cardamom, dried red chilli, cloves and nutmeg. Bezar Spice Blend contains none of the 14 major allergens and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

**Hashu Topping** (حشو) is spooned on top of Chicken Machboos (35 g). Slow-caramelised onions with golden raisins, ghee and a little bezar — the sweet-savoury crown of a traditional machboos. Hashu Topping is made from onion, golden raisins, ghee (clarified butter), sugar, green cardamom, salt and Bezar Spice Blend. Hashu Topping contains milk (dairy) and sulphites and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

**Dakkus Tomato-Chilli Sauce** (دقوس) is served on the side with Chicken Machboos (50 ml). The Gulf's classic tomato and chilli sauce, served on the side of every machboos so guests can add heat to taste. Dakkus Tomato-Chilli Sauce is made from tomato, tomato paste, garlic, green chilli, dried red chilli, lime, cumin, sunflower oil and salt. Dakkus Tomato-Chilli Sauce contains none of the 14 major allergens and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

section: Chicken Machboos: allergens
text:
## Chicken Machboos: allergens

Chicken Machboos contains milk (dairy) and sulphites as ingredients in its standard recipe. Where each allergen comes from:

- Milk (dairy): from the ghee and the Hashu Topping, which contains ghee
- Sulphites: from the Hashu Topping, which contains golden raisins

Chicken Machboos may contain traces of celery and mustard. Reasons:

- Ground spices are packed by a supplier that also handles mustard and celery.

Chicken Machboos contains no gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns and shrimp), molluscs, eggs, fish, peanuts, soy, tree nuts, sesame or lupin.

Kitchen allergen statement: Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

## Chicken Machboos: how spicy it is

Chicken Machboos is mild (spice level 1 of 3) as standard. Machboos is mild (warm spice rather than chilli heat) and cannot be made milder: the rice is cooked in stock seasoned with bezar. The heat comes from the dakkus served on the side, which can be skipped or doubled.

Can the spice be reduced? No. Can it be made spicier? Yes.

**Q: Can I get white meat only?**

A: Machboos is cooked with bone-in chicken quarters, so we cannot guarantee breast meat only.

**Q: How much is Chicken Machboos?**

A: Yes, Chicken Machboos can be delivered within Bayt Al Ghaf's delivery zones, 12:00 (noon) to 22:30 (10:30 pm).

A: Chicken Machboos takes about 15 minutes to prepare. For a pickup order, allow at least 25 minutes from ordering.

**Q: When can I order Chicken Machboos?**

A: Chicken Machboos is on the menu every day of the week. Chicken Machboos is served from 12:00 (noon) until the kitchen closes. A single regular order can include up to 10 Chicken Machboos.

section: What Muhammar with Fried Safi is
text:
## What Muhammar with Fried Safi is

A seafaring classic of the pearl-diving coast: basmati rice cooked with date syrup, sugar, saffron, cardamom and rosewater until amber and fragrant, served with a whole safi (rabbitfish) marinated in bezar and lime and fried until crisp. Dakkus on the side cuts the sweetness.

How Muhammar with Fried Safi is cooked: Rice steamed with date syrup; fish deep-fried in the dedicated seafood fryer. Style: Traditional coastal Emirati dish.

Guests also ask for Muhammar with Fried Safi as “muhammar”, “mhammar”, “sweet rice”, “date rice”, “safi” or “rabbitfish”. These are common spellings and descriptions of the same dish.

text:
## Questions guests ask about Muhammar with Fried Safi

**Q: Is muhammar sweet?**

A: Yes, the rice is gently sweet from date syrup and sugar, balanced by the salty fried fish and the tangy dakkus.

**Q: Can I have muhammar with chicken instead of fish?**

A: No, we only serve muhammar with safi. For chicken, try Chicken Machboos.

**Q: How much is Muhammar with Fried Safi?**

A: Muhammar with Fried Safi costs AED 69 (69 dirhams), including VAT.

**Q: How many people does Muhammar with Fried Safi serve?**

A: Muhammar with Fried Safi serves one person (about 600 g: one whole safi (about 300 g) and 150 g (dry) rice).

**Q: Is Muhammar with Fried Safi vegan?**

A: Muhammar with Fried Safi is not vegan; it is pescatarian (contains fish or seafood, no meat).

**Q: Does Muhammar with Fried Safi contain nuts?**

A: Muhammar with Fried Safi has no nut ingredients. The kitchen is not nut-free.

**Q: Does Muhammar with Fried Safi contain dairy?**

A: Yes, Muhammar with Fried Safi contains milk (dairy).

**Q: Is Muhammar with Fried Safi gluten-free?**

A: Muhammar with Fried Safi has no gluten-containing ingredients, but Bayt Al Ghaf is not a certified gluten-free kitchen.

**Q: How spicy is Muhammar with Fried Safi?**

A: Muhammar with Fried Safi is mild (spice level 1 of 3). The fish marinade is mild; dakkus adds heat.

**Q: Can I get Muhammar with Fried Safi delivered?**

A: Yes, Muhammar with Fried Safi can be delivered within Bayt Al Ghaf's delivery zones, 12:00 (noon) to 22:30 (10:30 pm).

**Q: How long does Muhammar with Fried Safi take?**

A: Muhammar with Fried Safi takes about 18 minutes to prepare. For a pickup order, allow at least 28 minutes from ordering.

**Q: When can I order Muhammar with Fried Safi?**

A: Muhammar with Fried Safi is on the menu every day of the week. Muhammar with Fried Safi is served from 12:00 (noon) until the kitchen closes. The kitchen makes a limited number of Muhammar with Fried Safi each day: 25 portions. Once they are gone, Muhammar with Fried Safi is sold out until the next day it is served.

section: What Camel Machboos (Thursday) is
text:
## What Camel Machboos (Thursday) is

A Thursday-night feast: young camel (hashi) shoulder braised slowly for three hours with loomi, onion, tomato and whole spices, then the basmati is cooked in the rich braising liquid with bezar. Topped with hashu and served with dakkus.

How Camel Machboos (Thursday) is cooked: Braised for 3 hours; rice steamed in the braising liquid. Style: Traditional Emirati festive machboos.

Guests also ask for Camel Machboos (Thursday) as “camel machboos”, “machboos laham ibil”, “camel rice” or “camel kabsa”. These are common spellings and descriptions of the same dish.

section: Camel Machboos (Thursday): sauces, marinades and spice blends
text:
## Camel Machboos (Thursday): sauces, marinades and spice blends

**Bezar Spice Blend** (بزار) is cooked into Camel Machboos (Thursday) (5 g). The Emirati house spice blend that seasons our machboos, saloona and grills. Whole spices are toasted and ground in-house every week. Bezar Spice Blend is made from coriander seed, cumin, fennel seed, black pepper, turmeric, cinnamon, green cardamom, dried red chilli, cloves and nutmeg. Bezar Spice Blend contains none of the 14 major allergens and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

**Hashu Topping** (حشو) is spooned on top of Camel Machboos (Thursday) (35 g). Slow-caramelised onions with golden raisins, ghee and a little bezar — the sweet-savoury crown of a traditional machboos. Hashu Topping is made from onion, golden raisins, ghee (clarified butter), sugar, green cardamom, salt and Bezar Spice Blend. Hashu Topping contains milk (dairy) and sulphites and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

**Dakkus Tomato-Chilli Sauce** (دقوس) is served on the side with Camel Machboos (Thursday) (50 ml). The Gulf's classic tomato and chilli sauce, served on the side of every machboos so guests can add heat to taste. Dakkus Tomato-Chilli Sauce is made from tomato, tomato paste, garlic, green chilli, dried red chilli, lime, cumin, sunflower oil and salt. Dakkus Tomato-Chilli Sauce contains none of the 14 major allergens and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

section: What Hammour Mashwi is
text:
## What Hammour Mashwi is

A thick fillet of hammour, the Gulf's most prized fish, marinated in bezar, lime, turmeric and garlic and grilled over charcoal until the skin crisps. Served with white basmati rice, a lime cheek and dakkus.

How Hammour Mashwi is cooked: Marinated for 30–60 minutes and grilled over charcoal. Style: Gulf seafood grill.

Guests also ask for Hammour Mashwi as “grilled hammour”, “hamour”, “grouper”, “grilled fish” or “hammour”. These are common spellings and descriptions of the same dish.

section: Hammour Mashwi: allergens
text:
## Hammour Mashwi: allergens

Hammour Mashwi contains fish as ingredients in its standard recipe. Where each allergen comes from:

- Fish: from the hammour (orange-spotted grouper) fillet

Hammour Mashwi may contain traces of gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns and shrimp), soy, celery, mustard and sesame. Reasons:

- Cooked on the shared charcoal grill used for lamb, camel, chicken, fish and prawns; some grill items are brushed with Sauce No. 7 (soy, wheat, sesame).
- Fish may contain small bones.
- Ground spices are packed by a supplier that also handles mustard and celery.

Hammour Mashwi contains no molluscs, eggs, peanuts, milk (dairy), tree nuts, sulphites or lupin.

Kitchen allergen statement: Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

text:
## Questions guests ask about Hammour Mashwi

**Q: Is the hammour fresh?**

A: Yes. We buy fresh hammour from licensed suppliers several times a week and only outside the UAE seasonal fishing ban. When we cannot source it, the dish is marked sold out.

**Q: Can I have it without spices?**

A: Yes — choose “Lime and salt only”.

**Q: How much is Hammour Mashwi?**

A: Hammour Mashwi costs AED 98 (98 dirhams), including VAT.

**Q: How many people does Hammour Mashwi serve?**

A: Hammour Mashwi serves one person (250 g hammour fillet (raw weight) with 120 g (dry) rice).

**Q: Is Hammour Mashwi vegan?**

A: Hammour Mashwi is not vegan; it is pescatarian (contains fish or seafood, no meat).

**Q: Does Hammour Mashwi contain nuts?**

A: Hammour Mashwi has no nut ingredients. The kitchen is not nut-free.

**Q: Does Hammour Mashwi contain dairy?**

A: Hammour Mashwi has no dairy ingredients.

**Q: Is Hammour Mashwi gluten-free?**

A: Hammour Mashwi has no gluten-containing ingredients, but Bayt Al Ghaf is not a certified gluten-free kitchen and this dish may contain traces of gluten.

**Q: How spicy is Hammour Mashwi?**

A: Hammour Mashwi is mild (spice level 1 of 3). The marinade is mild; the fish can be grilled with lime and salt only, or served with extra dakkus.

**Q: Can I get Hammour Mashwi delivered?**

A: Yes, Hammour Mashwi can be delivered within Bayt Al Ghaf's delivery zones, 12:00 (noon) to 22:30 (10:30 pm).

**Q: How long does Hammour Mashwi take?**

A: Hammour Mashwi takes about 20 minutes to prepare. For a pickup order, allow at least 30 minutes from ordering.

**Q: When can I order Hammour Mashwi?**

A: Hammour Mashwi is on the menu every day of the week. Hammour Mashwi is served from 12:00 (noon) until the kitchen closes. The kitchen makes a limited number of Hammour Mashwi each day: 25 portions. Once they are gone, Hammour Mashwi is sold out until the next day it is served.

section: Rubyan Mashwi: allergens
text:
## Rubyan Mashwi: allergens

Rubyan Mashwi contains crustaceans (prawns and shrimp) and milk (dairy) as ingredients in its standard recipe. Where each allergen comes from:

- Crustaceans (prawns and shrimp): from the gulf prawns
- Milk (dairy): from the Garlic Lime Butter, which contains butter

Rubyan Mashwi may contain traces of gluten (wheat), fish, soy, tree nuts, celery, mustard and sesame. Reasons:

- Cooked on the shared charcoal grill used for lamb, camel, chicken, fish and prawns; some grill items are brushed with Sauce No. 7 (soy, wheat, sesame).
- Made in the same blender and on the same station as Al Ghaf House Red, which contains walnuts and wheat; we cannot rule out traces of tree nuts or gluten.
- Ground spices are packed by a supplier that also handles mustard and celery.

Rubyan Mashwi contains no molluscs, eggs, peanuts, sulphites or lupin.

Kitchen allergen statement: Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

section: Rish Ghanam (Lamb Chops): sauces, marinades and spice blends
text:
## Rish Ghanam (Lamb Chops): sauces, marinades and spice blends

**Laban Marinade** (تتبيلة اللبن) is used as the marinade for Rish Ghanam (Lamb Chops). Yogurt marinade that tenderises our lamb chops overnight. Laban Marinade is made from natural yogurt, garlic, onion, lemon, olive oil, salt and Bezar Spice Blend. Laban Marinade contains milk (dairy) and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

**Sauce No. 7 (Saba'a)** (صلصة سبعة) is brushed as a glaze on Rish Ghanam (Lamb Chops) (20 ml). The chef's signature glaze, named for its seven key flavours: tamarind, date, soy, sesame, garlic, ginger and bezar. It contains soy, wheat (gluten, from the soy sauce) and sesame. Sauce No. 7 (Saba'a) is made from tamarind, date syrup (dibs), soy sauce, toasted sesame oil, garlic, ginger, loomi (dried black lime), sugar and Bezar Spice Blend. Sauce No. 7 (Saba'a) contains gluten (wheat), soy and sesame and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

**Toum Garlic Sauce** (ثومية) is served on the side with Rish Ghanam (Lamb Chops) (40 ml). Fluffy whipped garlic sauce made without egg or dairy. Toum Garlic Sauce is made from garlic, sunflower oil, lemon and salt. Toum Garlic Sauce contains none of the 14 major allergens.

section: Rish Ghanam (Lamb Chops): allergens
text:
## Rish Ghanam (Lamb Chops): allergens

Rish Ghanam (Lamb Chops) contains gluten (wheat), soy, milk (dairy) and sesame as ingredients in its standard recipe. Where each allergen comes from:

- Gluten (wheat): from the Sauce No. 7 (Saba'a), which contains soy sauce
- Soy: from the Sauce No. 7 (Saba'a), which contains soy sauce
- Milk (dairy): from the Laban Marinade, which contains natural yogurt
- Sesame: from the Sauce No. 7 (Saba'a), which contains toasted sesame oil

Rish Ghanam (Lamb Chops) may contain traces of crustaceans (prawns and shrimp), fish, celery and mustard. Reasons:

- Cooked on the shared charcoal grill used for lamb, camel, chicken, fish and prawns; some grill items are brushed with Sauce No. 7 (soy, wheat, sesame).
- Ground spices are packed by a supplier that also handles mustard and celery.

Rish Ghanam (Lamb Chops) contains no molluscs, eggs, peanuts, tree nuts, sulphites or lupin.

Kitchen allergen statement: Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

## What Saffron Shish Tawook is

Cubes of chicken breast marinated for six hours in yogurt, saffron, lemon and paprika, grilled on skewers with peppers and onion. Served with toum and your choice of rice or regag.

Guests also ask for Saffron Shish Tawook as “shish tawook”, “tawook”, “chicken skewers”, “chicken kebab” or “chicken tikka”. These are common spellings and descriptions of the same dish.

section: Saffron Shish Tawook: allergens
text:
## Saffron Shish Tawook: allergens

Saffron Shish Tawook contains milk (dairy) as ingredients in its standard recipe. Where each allergen comes from:

- Milk (dairy): from the Saffron Tawook Marinade, which contains natural yogurt

Saffron Shish Tawook may contain traces of gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns and shrimp), fish, soy and sesame. Reasons:

- Cooked on the shared charcoal grill used for lamb, camel, chicken, fish and prawns; some grill items are brushed with Sauce No. 7 (soy, wheat, sesame).

Saffron Shish Tawook contains no molluscs, eggs, peanuts, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sulphites or lupin.

Kitchen allergen statement: Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

Bezar Spice Blend is made from coriander seed, cumin, fennel seed, black pepper, turmeric, cinnamon, green cardamom, dried red chilli, cloves and nutmeg. **Al Ghaf House Red** (صلصة الغاف الحمراء) is served on the side with Camel Kofta (50 g). One of our two house sauces: a thick roasted-pepper and walnut sauce sharpened with pomegranate molasses. Al Ghaf House Red contains gluten (wheat) and tree nuts and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

section: Camel Kofta: allergens
text:
## Camel Kofta: allergens

Camel Kofta contains gluten (wheat) and tree nuts as ingredients in its standard recipe. Where each allergen comes from:

- Gluten (wheat): from the regag bread and the Al Ghaf House Red, which contains breadcrumbs
- Tree nuts: from the Al Ghaf House Red, which contains walnuts

Camel Kofta may contain traces of crustaceans (prawns and shrimp), fish, soy, celery, mustard and sesame. Reasons:

- Cooked on the shared charcoal grill used for lamb, camel, chicken, fish and prawns; some grill items are brushed with Sauce No. 7 (soy, wheat, sesame).
- Ground spices are packed by a supplier that also handles mustard and celery.

Camel Kofta contains no molluscs, eggs, peanuts, milk (dairy), sulphites or lupin.

Kitchen allergen statement: Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

## Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli: sauces, marinades and spice blends

**Sauce No. 7 (Saba'a)** (صلصة سبعة) is brushed as a glaze on Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli (15 ml). The chef's signature glaze, named for its seven key flavours: tamarind, date, soy, sesame, garlic, ginger and bezar. It contains soy, wheat (gluten, from the soy sauce) and sesame. Sauce No. 7 (Saba'a) is made from tamarind, date syrup (dibs), soy sauce, toasted sesame oil, garlic, ginger, loomi (dried black lime), sugar and Bezar Spice Blend. Sauce No. 7 (Saba'a) contains gluten (wheat), soy and sesame and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

**Loomi Aioli** (أيولي باللومي) is cooked into Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli (25 ml). House-made egg-yolk aioli seasoned with ground dried black lime. Loomi Aioli is made from egg yolk, rapeseed (canola) oil, loomi (dried black lime), garlic, lemon, dijon mustard and salt. Loomi Aioli contains eggs and mustard.

**Bezar Spice Blend** (بزار) is cooked into Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli (on the wedges). The Emirati house spice blend that seasons our machboos, saloona and grills. Whole spices are toasted and ground in-house every week. Bezar Spice Blend is made from coriander seed, cumin, fennel seed, black pepper, turmeric, cinnamon, green cardamom, dried red chilli, cloves and nutmeg. Bezar Spice Blend contains none of the 14 major allergens and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

text:
## Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli: allergens

Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli contains gluten (wheat), eggs, soy, milk (dairy), mustard and sesame as ingredients in its standard recipe. Where each allergen comes from:

- Gluten (wheat): from the brioche bun and the Sauce No. 7 (Saba'a), which contains soy sauce
- Eggs: from the brioche bun and the Loomi Aioli, which contains egg yolk
- Soy: from the Sauce No. 7 (Saba'a), which contains soy sauce
- Milk (dairy): from the brioche bun and the processed cheese
- Mustard: from the Loomi Aioli, which contains dijon mustard
- Sesame: from the brioche bun and the Sauce No. 7 (Saba'a), which contains toasted sesame oil

Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli may contain traces of crustaceans (prawns and shrimp), fish and celery. Reasons:

- Cooked on the shared charcoal grill used for lamb, camel, chicken, fish and prawns; some grill items are brushed with Sauce No. 7 (soy, wheat, sesame).
- Fried in the general fryer, which is shared with sambousa, luqaimat, khanfaroosh and potato wedges (wheat, milk, eggs and sesame).
- Ground spices are packed by a supplier that also handles mustard and celery.

Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli contains no molluscs, peanuts, tree nuts, sulphites or lupin.

Kitchen allergen statement: Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

text:
## Questions guests ask about Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli

**Q: Is the camel burger halal?**

A: Yes. All our meat, including camel, is halal.

**Q: Can the burger be made gluten-free?**

A: No. We do not have a gluten-free bun, and the wedges are fried in a shared fryer.

**Q: How much is Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli?**

A: Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli costs AED 72 (72 dirhams), including VAT.

**Q: How many people does Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli serve?**

A: Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli serves one person (180 g patty in a brioche bun with 150 g potato wedges).

**Q: Is Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli vegan?**

A: Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli is not vegan; it is a meat dish (contains halal meat or poultry).

**Q: Does Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli contain nuts?**

A: Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli has no nut ingredients. The kitchen is not nut-free.

**Q: Does Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli contain dairy?**

A: Yes, Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli contains milk (dairy).

**Q: Is Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli gluten-free?**

A: No, Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli contains gluten (wheat).

**Q: How spicy is Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli?**

A: Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli is mild (spice level 1 of 3). Order without Sauce No. 7 for no warmth, or add dakkus.

**Q: Can I get Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli delivered?**

A: Yes, Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli can be delivered within Bayt Al Ghaf's delivery zones, 12:00 (noon) to 22:30 (10:30 pm).

**Q: How long does Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli take?**

A: Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli takes about 15 minutes to prepare. For a pickup order, allow at least 25 minutes from ordering.

**Q: When can I order Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli?**

A: Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli is on the menu every day of the week. Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli is served from 12:00 (noon) until the kitchen closes. A single regular order can include up to 10 Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli.

text:
## What Vegetable Machboos is

All the warmth of machboos without the meat: chickpeas, potato, carrot, zucchini and eggplant cooked with onion, tomato, garlic, ginger and loomi, then basmati rice steamed in our vegetable stock with bezar and whole spices. Cooked with sunflower oil rather than ghee, so it is vegan. Served with dakkus.

How Vegetable Machboos is cooked: Vegetables braised; rice steamed in vegetable stock. Style: Emirati machboos, vegan.

Guests also ask for Vegetable Machboos as “vegetable majboos”, “veg machboos”, “vegan machboos”, “vegetable rice” or “vegetable kabsa”. These are common spellings and descriptions of the same dish.

text:
## Questions guests ask about Vegetable Machboos

**Q: Is the vegetable machboos vegan?**

A: Yes, as served it is vegan: cooked in sunflower oil and vegetable stock with no ghee. Adding hashu makes it vegetarian rather than vegan. It contains celery (in the stock).

**Q: How much is Vegetable Machboos?**

A: Vegetable Machboos costs AED 48 (48 dirhams), including VAT.

**Q: How many people does Vegetable Machboos serve?**

A: Vegetable Machboos serves one person (about 600 g with 150 g (dry) rice).

**Q: Is Vegetable Machboos vegan?**

A: Vegetable Machboos is vegan.

**Q: Does Vegetable Machboos contain nuts?**

A: Vegetable Machboos has no nut ingredients. The kitchen is not nut-free.

**Q: Does Vegetable Machboos contain dairy?**

A: Vegetable Machboos has no dairy ingredients.

**Q: Is Vegetable Machboos gluten-free?**

A: Vegetable Machboos has no gluten-containing ingredients, but Bayt Al Ghaf is not a certified gluten-free kitchen.

**Q: How spicy is Vegetable Machboos?**

A: Vegetable Machboos is mild (spice level 1 of 3). Mild; the rice is cooked in spiced stock. Add dakkus for heat.

**Q: Can I get Vegetable Machboos delivered?**

A: Yes, Vegetable Machboos can be delivered within Bayt Al Ghaf's delivery zones, 12:00 (noon) to 22:30 (10:30 pm).

**Q: How long does Vegetable Machboos take?**

A: Vegetable Machboos takes about 15 minutes to prepare. For a pickup order, allow at least 25 minutes from ordering.

**Q: When can I order Vegetable Machboos?**

A: Vegetable Machboos is on the menu every day of the week. Vegetable Machboos is served from 12:00 (noon) until the kitchen closes. A single regular order can include up to 10 Vegetable Machboos.

Chunks of orange pumpkin and chickpeas simmered with onion, tomato, ginger, garlic, turmeric, loomi and bezar in vegetable stock, finished with coriander. Served with white basmati rice.

section: Pumpkin & Chickpea Saloona: allergens
text:
## Pumpkin & Chickpea Saloona: allergens

Pumpkin & Chickpea Saloona contains celery as ingredients in its standard recipe. Where each allergen comes from:

- Celery: from the vegetable stock

Pumpkin & Chickpea Saloona may contain traces of mustard. Reasons:

- Ground spices are packed by a supplier that also handles mustard and celery.

Pumpkin & Chickpea Saloona contains no gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns and shrimp), molluscs, eggs, fish, peanuts, soy, milk (dairy), tree nuts, sesame, sulphites or lupin.

Kitchen allergen statement: Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

text:
## What Luqaimat is

The Emirates' favourite sweet: a light yeasted batter flavoured with saffron and cardamom, dropped by hand into hot oil, fried until crisp outside and fluffy inside, then drenched in warm date syrup and scattered with toasted sesame.

How Luqaimat is cooked: Deep-fried to order in the general fryer. Style: Traditional Emirati sweet.

Guests also ask for Luqaimat as “luqaimat”, “lugaimat”, “luqeimat”, “lokma”, “dumplings”, “sweet dumplings” or “date syrup balls”. These are common spellings and descriptions of the same dish.

section: Luqaimat: allergens
text:
## Luqaimat: allergens

Luqaimat contains gluten (wheat), milk (dairy) and sesame as ingredients in its standard recipe. Where each allergen comes from:

- Gluten (wheat): from the wheat flour
- Milk (dairy): from the milk powder
- Sesame: from the sesame seeds

Luqaimat may contain traces of eggs. Reasons:

- Fried in the general fryer, which is shared with sambousa, luqaimat, khanfaroosh and potato wedges (wheat, milk, eggs and sesame).

Luqaimat contains no crustaceans (prawns and shrimp), molluscs, fish, peanuts, soy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sulphites or lupin.

Kitchen allergen statement: Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

section: What Aseedat Bobar (Winter Pumpkin Asida) is
text:
## What Aseedat Bobar (Winter Pumpkin Asida) is

A winter tradition from Emirati grandmothers' kitchens: orange pumpkin (bobar) cooked down with toasted flour, sugar, saffron and cardamom, stirred with ghee until glossy and finished with a few drops of rosewater. Served warm.

How Aseedat Bobar (Winter Pumpkin Asida) is cooked: Stirred on the stove for 40 minutes. Style: Traditional Emirati winter sweet.

Guests also ask for Aseedat Bobar (Winter Pumpkin Asida) as “aseeda”, “asida”, “aseedat bobar”, “pumpkin asida”, “pumpkin pudding”, “winter dessert” or “seasonal dessert”. These are common spellings and descriptions of the same dish.

section: What Gahwa Emirati (Dallah for the Table) is
text:
## What Gahwa Emirati (Dallah for the Table) is

Emirati hospitality in a pot: lightly roasted Arabica beans brewed with cardamom, saffron and a hint of clove and rosewater, poured from a brass dallah into small finjan cups. Served with six Khalas dates. Gahwa is unsweetened and contains no milk.

How Gahwa Emirati (Dallah for the Table) is cooked: Brewed and simmered in the dallah. Style: Traditional Emirati coffee service.

Guests also ask for Gahwa Emirati (Dallah for the Table) as “gahwa”, “qahwa”, “kahwa”, “arabic coffee”, “emirati coffee”, “dallah” or “coffee”. These are common spellings and descriptions of the same dish.

text:
## Gahwa Emirati (Dallah for the Table): allergens

Gahwa Emirati (Dallah for the Table) contains none of the 14 major allergens as ingredients in its standard recipe.

Gahwa Emirati (Dallah for the Table) has no specific trace warnings beyond the general kitchen statement below.

Gahwa Emirati (Dallah for the Table) contains no gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns and shrimp), molluscs, eggs, fish, peanuts, soy, milk (dairy), tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites or lupin.

Kitchen allergen statement: Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

section: What Karak Chai is
text:
## What Karak Chai is

The UAE's everyday ritual: strong black tea boiled with evaporated milk, sugar, crushed cardamom and a few threads of saffron until rich and caramel-coloured.

How Karak Chai is cooked: Simmered. Style: Gulf karak.

Guests also ask for Karak Chai as “karak”, “chai karak”, “karak tea”, “masala tea”, “milk tea” or “chai”. These are common spellings and descriptions of the same dish.

section: Karak Chai: allergens
text:
## Karak Chai: allergens

Karak Chai contains milk (dairy) as ingredients in its standard recipe. Where each allergen comes from:

- Milk (dairy): from the evaporated milk

Karak Chai has no specific trace warnings beyond the general kitchen statement below.

Karak Chai contains no gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns and shrimp), molluscs, eggs, fish, peanuts, soy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites or lupin.

Kitchen allergen statement: Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

section: Questions guests ask about Karak Chai
text:
## Questions guests ask about Karak Chai

**Q: Can I have karak without dairy?**

A: No. Karak is made with evaporated milk (or camel milk). For a dairy-free tea, choose Sulaimani.

**Q: Can I have karak without sugar?**

A: Yes, choose “No sugar”.

**Q: How much is Karak Chai?**

A: Karak Chai costs AED 12 (12 dirhams), including VAT.

**Q: How many people does Karak Chai serve?**

A: Karak Chai serves one person (200 ml glass or takeaway cup).

**Q: Is Karak Chai vegan?**

A: Karak Chai is not vegan; it is vegetarian (contains dairy, eggs or honey, but no meat or fish).

**Q: Does Karak Chai contain nuts?**

A: Karak Chai has no nut ingredients. The kitchen is not nut-free.

**Q: Does Karak Chai contain dairy?**

A: Yes, Karak Chai contains milk (dairy).

**Q: Is Karak Chai gluten-free?**

A: Karak Chai has no gluten-containing ingredients, but Bayt Al Ghaf is not a certified gluten-free kitchen.

**Q: How spicy is Karak Chai?**

A: Karak Chai is not spicy (spice level 0 of 3). Not spicy.

**Q: Can I get Karak Chai delivered?**

A: Yes, Karak Chai can be delivered within Bayt Al Ghaf's delivery zones, 12:00 (noon) to 22:30 (10:30 pm).

**Q: How long does Karak Chai take?**

A: Karak Chai takes about 5 minutes to prepare. For a pickup order, allow at least 20 minutes from ordering.

**Q: When can I order Karak Chai?**

A: Karak Chai is on the menu every day of the week. Karak Chai is served all day, from opening at 08:00 (8 am) until the kitchen's last orders 30 minutes before closing. A single regular order can include up to 10 Karak Chai.

section: Majlis Sharing Platter: sauces, marinades and spice blends
text:
## Majlis Sharing Platter: sauces, marinades and spice blends

**Bezar Spice Blend** (بزار) is cooked into Majlis Sharing Platter. The Emirati house spice blend that seasons our machboos, saloona and grills. Whole spices are toasted and ground in-house every week. Bezar Spice Blend is made from coriander seed, cumin, fennel seed, black pepper, turmeric, cinnamon, green cardamom, dried red chilli, cloves and nutmeg. Bezar Spice Blend contains none of the 14 major allergens and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

**Hashu Topping** (حشو) is spooned on top of Majlis Sharing Platter. Slow-caramelised onions with golden raisins, ghee and a little bezar — the sweet-savoury crown of a traditional machboos. Hashu Topping is made from onion, golden raisins, ghee (clarified butter), sugar, green cardamom, salt and Bezar Spice Blend. Hashu Topping contains milk (dairy) and sulphites and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

**Dakkus Tomato-Chilli Sauce** (دقوس) is served on the side with Majlis Sharing Platter (150 ml). The Gulf's classic tomato and chilli sauce, served on the side of every machboos so guests can add heat to taste. Dakkus Tomato-Chilli Sauce is made from tomato, tomato paste, garlic, green chilli, dried red chilli, lime, cumin, sunflower oil and salt. Dakkus Tomato-Chilli Sauce contains none of the 14 major allergens and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

**Loomi & Sumac Dressing** (صلصة اللومي والسماق) is cooked into Majlis Sharing Platter. Olive-oil dressing with lime, ground loomi, sumac and pomegranate molasses. Loomi & Sumac Dressing is made from olive oil, lime, loomi (dried black lime), sumac, pomegranate molasses, salt and black pepper. Loomi & Sumac Dressing contains none of the 14 major allergens.

**Dibs (Date Syrup)** (دبس) is spooned on top of Majlis Sharing Platter (60 ml on the luqaimat). Pure date syrup from Emirati dates, served warm over luqaimat and chebab. Dibs (Date Syrup) is made from date syrup (dibs). Dibs (Date Syrup) contains none of the 14 major allergens.

section: Majlis Sharing Platter: allergens
text:
## Majlis Sharing Platter: allergens

Majlis Sharing Platter contains gluten (wheat), milk (dairy), sesame and sulphites as ingredients in its standard recipe. Where each allergen comes from:

- Gluten (wheat): from the sambousa pastry sheets and the wheat flour
- Milk (dairy): from the ghee, the white brined cheese, the milk powder and the Hashu Topping, which contains ghee
- Sesame: from the sesame seeds
- Sulphites: from the Hashu Topping, which contains golden raisins

Majlis Sharing Platter may contain traces of eggs, celery and mustard. Reasons:

- Fried in the general fryer, which is shared with sambousa, luqaimat, khanfaroosh and potato wedges (wheat, milk, eggs and sesame).
- Ground spices are packed by a supplier that also handles mustard and celery.

Majlis Sharing Platter contains no crustaceans (prawns and shrimp), molluscs, fish, peanuts, soy, tree nuts or lupin.

Kitchen allergen statement: Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

## What Friday Family Machboos Platter is

Friday lunch is family time in the Emirates. Our Friday tray carries a whole slow-braised lamb shoulder and a whole roast chicken over 750 g of spiced machboos rice with hashu, with dakkus, a large house salad, five laban and twenty luqaimat. Made only on Fridays in limited numbers.

How Friday Family Machboos Platter is cooked: Lamb braised for 3 hours; chicken roasted; rice steamed in the combined stock. Style: Emirati Friday family tray.

text:
## Friday Family Machboos Platter: sauces, marinades and spice blends

**Bezar Spice Blend** (بزار) is cooked into Friday Family Machboos Platter. The Emirati house spice blend that seasons our machboos, saloona and grills. Whole spices are toasted and ground in-house every week. Bezar Spice Blend is made from coriander seed, cumin, fennel seed, black pepper, turmeric, cinnamon, green cardamom, dried red chilli, cloves and nutmeg. Bezar Spice Blend contains none of the 14 major allergens and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

**Hashu Topping** (حشو) is spooned on top of Friday Family Machboos Platter. Slow-caramelised onions with golden raisins, ghee and a little bezar — the sweet-savoury crown of a traditional machboos. Hashu Topping is made from onion, golden raisins, ghee (clarified butter), sugar, green cardamom, salt and Bezar Spice Blend. Hashu Topping contains milk (dairy) and sulphites and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

**Dakkus Tomato-Chilli Sauce** (دقوس) is served on the side with Friday Family Machboos Platter (200 ml). The Gulf's classic tomato and chilli sauce, served on the side of every machboos so guests can add heat to taste. Dakkus Tomato-Chilli Sauce is made from tomato, tomato paste, garlic, green chilli, dried red chilli, lime, cumin, sunflower oil and salt. Dakkus Tomato-Chilli Sauce contains none of the 14 major allergens and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

**Loomi & Sumac Dressing** (صلصة اللومي والسماق) is cooked into Friday Family Machboos Platter. Olive-oil dressing with lime, ground loomi, sumac and pomegranate molasses. Loomi & Sumac Dressing is made from olive oil, lime, loomi (dried black lime), sumac, pomegranate molasses, salt and black pepper. Loomi & Sumac Dressing contains none of the 14 major allergens.

**Dibs (Date Syrup)** (دبس) is spooned on top of Friday Family Machboos Platter (60 ml on the luqaimat). Pure date syrup from Emirati dates, served warm over luqaimat and chebab. Dibs (Date Syrup) is made from date syrup (dibs). Dibs (Date Syrup) contains none of the 14 major allergens.

text:
## Friday Family Machboos Platter: allergens

Friday Family Machboos Platter contains gluten (wheat), milk (dairy), sesame and sulphites as ingredients in its standard recipe. Where each allergen comes from:

- Gluten (wheat): from the wheat flour
- Milk (dairy): from the ghee, the laban, the milk powder and the Hashu Topping, which contains ghee
- Sesame: from the sesame seeds
- Sulphites: from the Hashu Topping, which contains golden raisins

Friday Family Machboos Platter may contain traces of eggs, celery and mustard. Reasons:

- Fried in the general fryer, which is shared with sambousa, luqaimat, khanfaroosh and potato wedges (wheat, milk, eggs and sesame).
- Ground spices are packed by a supplier that also handles mustard and celery.

Friday Family Machboos Platter contains no crustaceans (prawns and shrimp), molluscs, fish, peanuts, soy, tree nuts or lupin.

Kitchen allergen statement: Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

text:
## What Whole Lamb Ouzi is

The centrepiece of Emirati celebrations: a whole young lamb marinated in bezar and loomi and slow-roasted for six hours, served on 2.5 kg of spiced basmati with hashu, fried almonds and pine nuts. Comes with dakkus and a large house salad. Ordered through our catering team with at least 48 hours' notice.

How Whole Lamb Ouzi is cooked: Marinated overnight and slow-roasted for 6 hours. Style: Emirati celebration dish.

Guests also ask for Whole Lamb Ouzi as “ouzi”, “quzi”, “ghuzi”, “whole lamb”, “roast lamb” or “kharoof”. These are common spellings and descriptions of the same dish.

section: Whole Lamb Ouzi: sauces, marinades and spice blends
text:
## Whole Lamb Ouzi: sauces, marinades and spice blends

**Bezar Spice Blend** (بزار) is used as the marinade for Whole Lamb Ouzi. The Emirati house spice blend that seasons our machboos, saloona and grills. Whole spices are toasted and ground in-house every week. Bezar Spice Blend is made from coriander seed, cumin, fennel seed, black pepper, turmeric, cinnamon, green cardamom, dried red chilli, cloves and nutmeg. Bezar Spice Blend contains none of the 14 major allergens and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

**Hashu Topping** (حشو) is spooned on top of Whole Lamb Ouzi. Slow-caramelised onions with golden raisins, ghee and a little bezar — the sweet-savoury crown of a traditional machboos. Hashu Topping is made from onion, golden raisins, ghee (clarified butter), sugar, green cardamom, salt and Bezar Spice Blend. Hashu Topping contains milk (dairy) and sulphites and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

**Dakkus Tomato-Chilli Sauce** (دقوس) is served on the side with Whole Lamb Ouzi (500 ml). The Gulf's classic tomato and chilli sauce, served on the side of every machboos so guests can add heat to taste. Dakkus Tomato-Chilli Sauce is made from tomato, tomato paste, garlic, green chilli, dried red chilli, lime, cumin, sunflower oil and salt. Dakkus Tomato-Chilli Sauce contains none of the 14 major allergens and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

**Loomi & Sumac Dressing** (صلصة اللومي والسماق) is cooked into Whole Lamb Ouzi. Olive-oil dressing with lime, ground loomi, sumac and pomegranate molasses. Loomi & Sumac Dressing is made from olive oil, lime, loomi (dried black lime), sumac, pomegranate molasses, salt and black pepper. Loomi & Sumac Dressing contains none of the 14 major allergens.
