section: Whole Lamb Ouzi: allergens
text:
## Whole Lamb Ouzi: allergens

Whole Lamb Ouzi contains milk (dairy), tree nuts and sulphites as ingredients in its standard recipe. Where each allergen comes from:

- Milk (dairy): from the ghee and the Hashu Topping, which contains ghee
- Tree nuts: from the almonds and the pine nuts
- Sulphites: from the Hashu Topping, which contains golden raisins

Whole Lamb Ouzi may contain traces of celery and mustard. Reasons:

- Ground spices are packed by a supplier that also handles mustard and celery.

Whole Lamb Ouzi contains no gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns and shrimp), molluscs, eggs, fish, peanuts, soy, sesame or lupin.

Kitchen allergen statement: Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

text:
## Questions guests ask about Whole Lamb Ouzi

**Q: How many people does a whole lamb ouzi feed?**

A: 10 to 12 adults as the main dish.

**Q: Can I order an ouzi for tonight?**

A: No. Each lamb is ordered from the butcher and marinated overnight, so we need at least 48 hours' notice.

**Q: Does the ouzi contain nuts?**

A: Yes, it is garnished with fried almonds and pine nuts. You can request no nut garnish, but the kitchen handles nuts.

**Q: How much is Whole Lamb Ouzi?**

A: Whole Lamb Ouzi costs AED 1,450 (1450 dirhams), including VAT.

**Q: How many people does Whole Lamb Ouzi serve?**

A: Whole Lamb Ouzi serves 10 people (serves 10–12: one whole lamb (8–9 kg dressed weight) on 2.5 kg (dry) rice).

**Q: Is Whole Lamb Ouzi vegan?**

A: Whole Lamb Ouzi is not vegan; it is a meat dish (contains halal meat or poultry).

**Q: Does Whole Lamb Ouzi contain nuts?**

A: Yes. Whole Lamb Ouzi contains tree nuts.

**Q: Does Whole Lamb Ouzi contain dairy?**

A: Yes, Whole Lamb Ouzi contains milk (dairy).

**Q: Is Whole Lamb Ouzi gluten-free?**

A: Whole Lamb Ouzi has no gluten-containing ingredients, but Bayt Al Ghaf is not a certified gluten-free kitchen.

**Q: How spicy is Whole Lamb Ouzi?**

A: Whole Lamb Ouzi is mild (spice level 1 of 3). Mild; extra dakkus can be supplied.

**Q: Can I get Whole Lamb Ouzi delivered?**

A: Yes, Whole Lamb Ouzi can be delivered within Bayt Al Ghaf's delivery zones, 12:00 (noon) to 22:30 (10:30 pm).

**Q: How long does Whole Lamb Ouzi take?**

A: Whole Lamb Ouzi takes about 480 minutes to prepare. For a pickup order, allow at least 490 minutes from ordering.

**Q: When can I order Whole Lamb Ouzi?**

A: Whole Lamb Ouzi is on the menu every day of the week. Whole Lamb Ouzi is served all day, from opening at 08:00 (8 am) until the kitchen's last orders 30 minutes before closing. The kitchen makes a limited number of Whole Lamb Ouzi each day: 3 portions. Once they are gone, Whole Lamb Ouzi is sold out until the next day it is served.

section: Office Machboos Lunch Box: sauces, marinades and spice blends
text:
## Office Machboos Lunch Box: sauces, marinades and spice blends

**Bezar Spice Blend** (بزار) is cooked into Office Machboos Lunch Box. The Emirati house spice blend that seasons our machboos, saloona and grills. Whole spices are toasted and ground in-house every week. Bezar Spice Blend is made from coriander seed, cumin, fennel seed, black pepper, turmeric, cinnamon, green cardamom, dried red chilli, cloves and nutmeg. Bezar Spice Blend contains none of the 14 major allergens and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

**Hashu Topping** (حشو) is spooned on top of Office Machboos Lunch Box. Slow-caramelised onions with golden raisins, ghee and a little bezar — the sweet-savoury crown of a traditional machboos. Hashu Topping is made from onion, golden raisins, ghee (clarified butter), sugar, green cardamom, salt and Bezar Spice Blend. Hashu Topping contains milk (dairy) and sulphites and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

**Dakkus Tomato-Chilli Sauce** (دقوس) is served on the side with Office Machboos Lunch Box (40 ml). The Gulf's classic tomato and chilli sauce, served on the side of every machboos so guests can add heat to taste. Dakkus Tomato-Chilli Sauce is made from tomato, tomato paste, garlic, green chilli, dried red chilli, lime, cumin, sunflower oil and salt. Dakkus Tomato-Chilli Sauce contains none of the 14 major allergens and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

**Loomi & Sumac Dressing** (صلصة اللومي والسماق) is cooked into Office Machboos Lunch Box. Olive-oil dressing with lime, ground loomi, sumac and pomegranate molasses. Loomi & Sumac Dressing is made from olive oil, lime, loomi (dried black lime), sumac, pomegranate molasses, salt and black pepper. Loomi & Sumac Dressing contains none of the 14 major allergens.

**Dibs (Date Syrup)** (دبس) is served on the side with Office Machboos Lunch Box (15 ml). Pure date syrup from Emirati dates, served warm over luqaimat and chebab. Dibs (Date Syrup) is made from date syrup (dibs). Dibs (Date Syrup) contains none of the 14 major allergens.

section: Office Machboos Lunch Box: allergens
text:
## Office Machboos Lunch Box: allergens

Office Machboos Lunch Box contains gluten (wheat), milk (dairy), sesame and sulphites as ingredients in its standard recipe. Where each allergen comes from:

- Gluten (wheat): from the wheat flour
- Milk (dairy): from the ghee, the milk powder and the Hashu Topping, which contains ghee
- Sesame: from the sesame seeds
- Sulphites: from the Hashu Topping, which contains golden raisins

Office Machboos Lunch Box may contain traces of eggs, celery and mustard. Reasons:

- Fried in the general fryer, which is shared with sambousa, luqaimat, khanfaroosh and potato wedges (wheat, milk, eggs and sesame).
- Ground spices are packed by a supplier that also handles mustard and celery.

Office Machboos Lunch Box contains no crustaceans (prawns and shrimp), molluscs, fish, peanuts, soy, tree nuts or lupin.

Kitchen allergen statement: Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

text:
## Questions guests ask about Office Machboos Lunch Box

**Q: Can I order 40 lunch boxes for my office tomorrow?**

A: Yes, if the order is placed at least 24 hours before the delivery or collection time and catering capacity is available that day. Request a quote for the exact time and our catering team confirms it.

**Q: Can I mix chicken and vegetarian boxes?**

A: Yes. Add one line per main (for example 30 chicken and 10 vegetable); the 10-box minimum applies to each line.

**Q: How much is Office Machboos Lunch Box?**

A: Office Machboos Lunch Box costs AED 45 (45 dirhams), including VAT.

**Q: How many people does Office Machboos Lunch Box serve?**

A: Office Machboos Lunch Box serves one person (one box: machboos (150 g dry rice with chicken/lamb/vegetables), 120 g salad, 3 luqaimat, 330 ml water).

**Q: Is Office Machboos Lunch Box vegan?**

A: Office Machboos Lunch Box is not vegan; it is a meat dish (contains halal meat or poultry).

**Q: Does Office Machboos Lunch Box contain nuts?**

A: Office Machboos Lunch Box has no nut ingredients. The kitchen is not nut-free.

**Q: Does Office Machboos Lunch Box contain dairy?**

A: Yes, Office Machboos Lunch Box contains milk (dairy).

**Q: Is Office Machboos Lunch Box gluten-free?**

A: No, Office Machboos Lunch Box contains gluten (wheat).

**Q: How spicy is Office Machboos Lunch Box?**

A: Office Machboos Lunch Box is mild (spice level 1 of 3). Mild; dakkus is packed on the side.

**Q: Can I get Office Machboos Lunch Box delivered?**

A: Yes, Office Machboos Lunch Box can be delivered within Bayt Al Ghaf's delivery zones, 12:00 (noon) to 22:30 (10:30 pm).

**Q: How long does Office Machboos Lunch Box take?**

A: Office Machboos Lunch Box takes about 240 minutes to prepare. For a pickup order, allow at least 250 minutes from ordering.

**Q: When can I order Office Machboos Lunch Box?**

A: Office Machboos Lunch Box is on the menu every day of the week. Office Machboos Lunch Box is served all day, from opening at 08:00 (8 am) until the kitchen's last orders 30 minutes before closing. The kitchen makes a limited number of Office Machboos Lunch Box each day: 150 portions. Once they are gone, Office Machboos Lunch Box is sold out until the next day it is served.

text:
## Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person): sauces, marinades and spice blends

**Bezar Spice Blend** (بزار) is cooked into Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person). The Emirati house spice blend that seasons our machboos, saloona and grills. Whole spices are toasted and ground in-house every week. Bezar Spice Blend is made from coriander seed, cumin, fennel seed, black pepper, turmeric, cinnamon, green cardamom, dried red chilli, cloves and nutmeg. Bezar Spice Blend contains none of the 14 major allergens and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

**Hashu Topping** (حشو) is spooned on top of Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person). Slow-caramelised onions with golden raisins, ghee and a little bezar — the sweet-savoury crown of a traditional machboos. Hashu Topping is made from onion, golden raisins, ghee (clarified butter), sugar, green cardamom, salt and Bezar Spice Blend. Hashu Topping contains milk (dairy) and sulphites and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

**Dakkus Tomato-Chilli Sauce** (دقوس) is served on the side with Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person). The Gulf's classic tomato and chilli sauce, served on the side of every machboos so guests can add heat to taste. Dakkus Tomato-Chilli Sauce is made from tomato, tomato paste, garlic, green chilli, dried red chilli, lime, cumin, sunflower oil and salt. Dakkus Tomato-Chilli Sauce contains none of the 14 major allergens and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

**Dibs (Date Syrup)** (دبس) is spooned on top of Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person). Pure date syrup from Emirati dates, served warm over luqaimat and chebab. Dibs (Date Syrup) is made from date syrup (dibs). Dibs (Date Syrup) contains none of the 14 major allergens.

section: Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person): allergens
text:
## Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person): allergens

Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person) contains gluten (wheat), milk (dairy), celery, sesame and sulphites as ingredients in its standard recipe. Where each allergen comes from:

- Gluten (wheat): from the sourdough croutons, the sambousa pastry sheets and the wheat flour
- Milk (dairy): from the laban, the white brined cheese, the ghee, the milk powder, the evaporated milk and the Hashu Topping, which contains ghee
- Celery: from the vegetable stock and the celery
- Sesame: from the sesame seeds
- Sulphites: from the Hashu Topping, which contains golden raisins

Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person) may contain traces of eggs and mustard. Reasons:

- Fried in the general fryer, which is shared with sambousa, luqaimat, khanfaroosh and potato wedges (wheat, milk, eggs and sesame).
- Ground spices are packed by a supplier that also handles mustard and celery.

Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person) contains no crustaceans (prawns and shrimp), molluscs, fish, peanuts, soy, tree nuts or lupin.

Kitchen allergen statement: Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

A: No. The Iftar Set Menu is only served during Ramadan. Outside Ramadan, many of the same dishes are on the regular menu: Shorbat Adas, sambousa, machboos, harees and luqaimat.

A: We seat iftar guests from 17:30 and serve dates and laban at the sunset call to prayer. Pickup sets can be collected between 17:30 and 20:30.

**Q: Can I order iftar for one person?**

A: The minimum is two sets per order or table.

A: Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person) costs AED 125 (125 dirhams), including VAT.

A: Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person) serves one person (per person: 3 dates, 200 ml laban, 250 ml soup, 2 sambousa, 1 main, 5 luqaimat, 1 tea).

**Q: Does Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person) contain dairy?**

A: Yes, Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person) contains milk (dairy).

**Q: Is Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person) gluten-free?**

A: No, Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person) contains gluten (wheat).

**Q: How spicy is Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person)?**

A: Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person) is mild (spice level 1 of 3). Mild; dakkus is served on the side.

**Q: Can I get Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person) delivered?**

A: No, Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person) is not delivered. It can be ordered for dine-in, pickup (takeaway) or dine-in pre-order.

**Q: How long does Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person) take?**

A: Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person) takes about 20 minutes to prepare. For a pickup order, allow at least 30 minutes from ordering.

Slow-caramelised onions with golden raisins, ghee and a little bezar — the sweet-savoury crown of a traditional machboos. Hashu Topping is made from onion, golden raisins, ghee (clarified butter), sugar, green cardamom, salt and Bezar Spice Blend. Hashu Topping contains milk (dairy) and sulphites and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

Dakkus Tomato-Chilli Sauce is made from tomato, tomato paste, garlic, green chilli, dried red chilli, lime, cumin, sunflower oil and salt. Dakkus Tomato-Chilli Sauce contains none of the 14 major allergens and may contain traces of celery and mustard.

**Dibs (Date Syrup)** (دبس) is spooned on top of Eid Al Etihad Feast (National Day). Pure date syrup from Emirati dates, served warm over luqaimat and chebab. Dibs (Date Syrup) is made from date syrup (dibs). Dibs (Date Syrup) contains none of the 14 major allergens.

**Loomi & Sumac Dressing** (صلصة اللومي والسماق) is cooked into Eid Al Etihad Feast (National Day). Olive-oil dressing with lime, ground loomi, sumac and pomegranate molasses. text:
## Eid Al Etihad Feast (National Day): allergens

Eid Al Etihad Feast (National Day) contains gluten (wheat), eggs, milk (dairy), sesame and sulphites as ingredients in its standard recipe. Where each allergen comes from:

- Gluten (wheat): from the hulled wheat and the wheat flour
- Eggs: from the eggs
- Milk (dairy): from the ghee, the full-cream milk, the milk powder and the Hashu Topping, which contains ghee
- Sesame: from the sesame seeds
- Sulphites: from the Hashu Topping, which contains golden raisins

Eid Al Etihad Feast (National Day) may contain traces of celery and mustard. Reasons:

- Ground spices are packed by a supplier that also handles mustard and celery.

Eid Al Etihad Feast (National Day) contains no crustaceans (prawns and shrimp), molluscs, fish, peanuts, soy, tree nuts or lupin.

Kitchen allergen statement: Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

text:
## Hashu Topping at a glance

Hashu Topping (Arabic: حشو) is a topping made in the Bayt Al Ghaf kitchen. Slow-caramelised onions with golden raisins, ghee and a little bezar — the sweet-savoury crown of a traditional machboos.

- Type: topping
- House preparation: no
- Flavour: Sweet, buttery and gently spiced
- Spice: not spicy (spice level 0 of 3)
- Contains allergens: milk (dairy) and sulphites

- Diet: vegetarian (contains dairy, eggs or honey, but no meat or fish)

- Extra portion: AED 5 where offered as an extra
- Also called: hashu, hashwa, fried onion raisin topping

section: Recipe of Hashu Topping: every ingredient with quantities
text:
## Recipe of Hashu Topping: every ingredient with quantities

One batch of Hashu Topping yields about 10 portions (35 g each) and is made from:

- Onion: 500 g, thinly sliced
- Golden raisins: 80 g (contains sulphites)
- Ghee (clarified butter): 40 g (contains milk (dairy))
- Sugar: 10 g
- Green cardamom: 2 g, ground
- Salt: 3 g
- Bezar Spice Blend: 3 g (a Bayt Al Ghaf preparation with its own recipe)

Hashu Topping includes Bezar Spice Blend, so everything in Bezar Spice Blend is also in Hashu Topping.

## How Hashu Topping is made

Onions are cooked slowly in ghee for about 45 minutes until deep golden, then raisins, sugar, cardamom and a pinch of bezar are folded through.

Batch size: about 10 portions (35 g each). Hashu Topping is served warm.

## Sauce No. 7 (Saba'a) at a glance

Sauce No. 7 (Saba'a) (Arabic: صلصة سبعة) is a glaze made in the Bayt Al Ghaf kitchen and one of its named house preparations. The chef's signature glaze, named for its seven key flavours: tamarind, date, soy, sesame, garlic, ginger and bezar. It contains soy, wheat (gluten, from the soy sauce) and sesame.

- Type: glaze
- House preparation: yes
- Flavour: Sticky, sweet-sour and deeply savoury with a mild warmth
- Spice: mild (spice level 1 of 3)
- Contains allergens: gluten (wheat), soy and sesame
- May contain traces of: celery and mustard
- Diet: vegan (no animal products)
- Served: Brushed hot onto grills; also served warm as a dip
- Used in: Rish Ghanam (Lamb Chops) and Camel Burger with Loomi Aioli
- Extra portion: AED 5 where offered as an extra
- Also called: sauce no 7, sauce number seven, saba'a, sabaa sauce, house glaze, seven sauce

section: Advice for guests avoiding gluten (wheat) at Bayt Al Ghaf
text:
## Advice for guests avoiding gluten (wheat) at Bayt Al Ghaf

- Regag, chebab, sambousa pastry, harees wheat, vermicelli (balaleet), margooga dough, croutons, breadcrumbs and the brioche bun all contain wheat.
- Sauce No. 7 contains soy sauce, which is brewed with wheat, so dishes glazed with Sauce No. 7 contain gluten.
- No dish is certified gluten-free. Wheat flour is handled throughout the kitchen and the general fryer is shared.

Bayt Al Ghaf never describes a dish as completely free from gluten (wheat) or any other allergen, because all food is prepared in one shared kitchen. Guests with a severe gluten (wheat) allergy should speak to the duty manager before ordering, and mention the allergy in the order notes so the team can call back.

text:
## Advice for guests avoiding milk (dairy) at Bayt Al Ghaf

- Ghee (clarified butter) is a dairy product. It is used in machboos, harees, balaleet, the hashu topping and many sweets.
- Camel milk (in the camel milk ice cream and as an option in karak and the date shake) is still milk and contains lactose.
- Laban and the saffron yoghurt sauce are dairy.

Bayt Al Ghaf never describes a dish as completely free from milk (dairy) or any other allergen, because all food is prepared in one shared kitchen. Guests with a severe milk (dairy) allergy should speak to the duty manager before ordering, and mention the allergy in the order notes so the team can call back.

## Tree nuts at Bayt Al Ghaf: summary

Tree nuts are used as an ingredient in the Bayt Al Ghaf kitchen. 4 dishes contain tree nuts in the standard recipe, 2 dishes may contain traces, and 42 dishes have no tree nuts in their ingredients.

Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

section: Bayt Al Ghaf kitchen allergen statement
text:
## Bayt Al Ghaf kitchen allergen statement

Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

section: How Bayt Al Ghaf answers allergy questions
text:
## How Bayt Al Ghaf answers allergy questions

- Staff say what a dish contains as ingredients and what it may contain as traces, using the recipe of that exact dish and any options chosen.
- Bayt Al Ghaf never says a dish is “safe”, “allergen-free” or “100% free” of an allergen, and never guarantees there is no cross-contamination, because there is one shared kitchen.
- Guests with a severe allergy (anaphylaxis, an EpiPen, coeliac disease) are asked to speak to the duty manager before ordering. Allergies written in order notes are flagged and the duty manager calls the guest back.
- Leaving an ingredient out (for example “no sesame seeds”) removes it from the recipe, not from the kitchen, so a trace warning still applies.
- Bayt Al Ghaf cannot cook any dish in a separate allergen-free kitchen, and cannot make the whole menu free from any allergen.
- All meat and poultry are halal; no pork, alcohol or gelatine is used.

document_title: How ordering works at Bayt Al Ghaf
section: Ways to order from Bayt Al Ghaf
text:
## Ways to order from Bayt Al Ghaf

- Pickup (takeaway): order ahead and collect at the takeaway counter at Heritage Quarter Gate 3, Al Seef Street, at the confirmed time.
- Delivery: Bayt Al Ghaf's own drivers deliver within central Dubai, with arrival between 12:00 (noon) to 22:30 (10:30 pm).
- Dine-in pre-order: order before arriving so the food is ready when you sit down. It needs a confirmed table reservation made with the same phone number.
- Guests can always order at the table without a pre-order, and can order takeaway without a reservation.
- Orders can be placed by phone on +971 4 555 0142 or on the Bayt Al Ghaf website.

section: Details Bayt Al Ghaf needs for an order
text:
## Details Bayt Al Ghaf needs for an order

- The customer's name and a valid phone number (UAE local format such as 050 123 4567, or international with the country code). Delivery orders need a UAE mobile number so the driver can call.
- The dishes, quantities and any options (for example spice level or “no raisins”).
- A pickup time, a delivery time, or ASAP (as soon as possible).
- For delivery only: the area, the building or villa, the street, and the apartment or floor if there is one. A landmark, Makani number and instructions help but are optional. No address is needed for pickup.
- Optional: an e-mail address, the name of someone else who will collect, and special instructions (up to 300 characters).

## When a Bayt Al Ghaf order is confirmed

An order is confirmed only when Bayt Al Ghaf has accepted it, and the customer receives an order number such as ORD-482913 (catering orders start with CAT-).

Most orders are confirmed straight away. These are received as “awaiting confirmation” and confirmed by the team by phone: orders above AED 1,500; orders from phone numbers with 2 or more uncollected orders in the last 90 days; and every catering order.

section: How long Bayt Al Ghaf holds a pickup order
text:
## How long Bayt Al Ghaf holds a pickup order

Pickup orders are held for 60 minutes after the pickup time. Hot food is kept warm for about 30 minutes. After 60 minutes an uncollected order is marked “not collected” and is not kept, for food-safety reasons. Customers running late should call +971 4 555 0142 so the order can be re-timed if the kitchen has not started it.

section: Bayt Al Ghaf lead-time rule
text:
## Bayt Al Ghaf lead-time rule

The earliest an order can be ready is the longest preparation time in the order plus 10 minutes for packing, and never less than 20 minutes after ordering. For example, an order with Hammour Mashwi (20 minutes) needs at least 30 minutes; an order of only Shorbat Adas (8 minutes) needs at least 20 minutes.

A delivery time is the time the food arrives. The kitchen starts the order early enough to cover the drive: 15 minutes to Zone A — Old Dubai, 25 minutes to Zone B — Creek & Deira and 35 minutes to Zone C — Downtown & Garhoud. The earliest delivery is therefore the lead time plus the drive time; for a dish that needs 25 minutes, delivery to Zone B is at the earliest 50 minutes after ordering. Arrival is estimated within a 15-minute window.

section: Bayt Al Ghaf delivery in brief
text:
## Bayt Al Ghaf delivery in brief

Bayt Al Ghaf delivers with its own drivers in Dubai, with arrival between 12:00 (noon) to 22:30 (10:30 pm) every day. Regular orders are delivered to Zone A — Old Dubai, Zone B — Creek & Deira and Zone C — Downtown & Garhoud; Zone D — Greater Dubai (catering only) is for catering orders only. Bayt Al Ghaf does not deliver outside Dubai — not to Abu Dhabi, Sharjah, Ajman or the other emirates — and is not on third-party delivery apps.

section: Bayt Al Ghaf delivery rules
text:
## Bayt Al Ghaf delivery rules

- A UAE mobile number is required so the driver can call.
- The address needs the area (which must be in a delivery zone), the building or villa and the street, plus the apartment or floor if there is one. A landmark, Makani number and instructions are welcome.
- The delivery time is when the food arrives; arrival is estimated within a 15-minute window.
- The earliest delivery is the preparation lead time plus the drive time for the zone. No delivery can be faster than that.
- Payment is cash or card on delivery. Drivers carry change up to AED 200.
- If the driver cannot reach the customer at the address within 10 minutes, the delivery is marked as failed and the team calls.
- Breakfast is not delivered.

section: Bayt Al Ghaf reservation rules in brief
text:
## Bayt Al Ghaf reservation rules in brief

- Tables can be booked for 1 to 20 guests.
- Bookings can be made from 30 minutes ahead up to 60 days ahead, on 15-minute times (for example 19:00, 19:15, 19:30).
- Groups of up to 12 are confirmed immediately when a table is free.
- Groups of 13 to 20 are accepted as a request: a table is held and the team calls back to confirm, usually within 4 hours.
- Groups of more than 20 cannot be booked as a normal reservation; contact the events team at events@baytalghaf.example.
- A name and a phone number are needed for every reservation (UAE number, or international with the country code).
- Bookings are made by phone on +971 4 555 0142, on the Bayt Al Ghaf website, or by e-mail to reservations@baytalghaf.example.
- Every booking gets a reference such as RES-482913.

section: Choosing where to sit at Bayt Al Ghaf
text:
## Choosing where to sit at Bayt Al Ghaf

- Guests can ask for the main dining hall (indoor), a creek-view window table, the creek terrace (seasonal) or a private majlis room.
- A requested seating area is respected: if it is full, the team offers other times or another area. Guests are never moved to a different area without being asked.
- With no preference, the team chooses the best-fitting table: the main hall first, then the terrace (in season), then the window tables.
- A specific table number cannot be promised.
- If the window tables are fully booked, one cannot be “made available”; the team offers another time with window availability or a different area.

section: Wheelchairs, high chairs and children at Bayt Al Ghaf
text:
## Wheelchairs, high chairs and children at Bayt Al Ghaf

- Mention a wheelchair when booking and only step-free, accessible tables are offered (in the main hall, at the window and on the terrace at T4 and T6). The majlis rooms have floor seating.
- Up to 4 high chairs can be requested per booking (6 in the restaurant).
- Children count towards the party size.

section: Private majlis room (floor seating) at Bayt Al Ghaf
text:
## Private majlis room (floor seating) at Bayt Al Ghaf

Two private majlis rooms with traditional floor seating: Majlis Al Sidr (6 to 10 guests; low chairs on request) and Majlis Al Ghaf (10 to 20 guests). A majlis booking needs at least 6 guests and 24 hours' notice, lasts 180 minutes, and has a minimum spend of AED 150 per person, settled at the end of the meal.

This area has 2 tables for parties of 6 to 20 guests.

section: Group bookings at Bayt Al Ghaf
text:
## Group bookings at Bayt Al Ghaf

- Up to 12 guests: confirmed instantly if a table is free.
- 13 to 20 guests: a table is held and the booking is a request until the team calls back, usually within 4 hours.
- More than 20 guests: not bookable as a reservation — contact the events team at events@baytalghaf.example.
- Book for the number of guests expected. If numbers are uncertain, book the likely number and update it before the change cut-off; tables for large groups may be reduced if far fewer guests arrive.

section: How a Bayt Al Ghaf catering order works
text:
## How a Bayt Al Ghaf catering order works

- 1. The customer asks for a catering quote with the dishes, quantities, date and time, and pickup or delivery area. The quote checks notice, capacity, delivery and price.
- 2. A quote is valid for 48 hours and locks the price.
- 3. The customer places the catering order from the quote. It is received as “awaiting confirmation” with a number starting CAT-.
- 4. The catering team calls to confirm within 4 hours and arranges any deposit. The order is only confirmed after that call.

- 21 to 60 portions: at least 24 hours' notice
- 61 to 150 portions: at least 48 hours' notice
- 151 to 250 portions: at least 72 hours' notice

Some dishes need more notice than the tier: Harees (48 hours), Camel Machboos (Thursday) (72 hours), Camel Kofta (48 hours), Whole Lamb Ouzi (48 hours) and Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person) (24 hours). The longest requirement applies.

section: Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person): only during Ramadan
text:
## Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person): only during Ramadan

Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person) (سفرة الإفطار) costs AED 125 and serves 1. Break your fast the Emirati way. Each set includes three Khalas dates with laban, Shorbat Adas, two sambousa, a main of your choice (lamb machboos, chicken machboos, harees or vegetable machboos), five luqaimat with dibs, and karak or sulaimani. Minimum two sets per order or table.

- Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person) is on the menu every day of the week.
- Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person) is served from 17:30 (5:30 pm) until 20:30 (8:30 pm).
- Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person) is available only during Ramadan.
- Same-day orders for Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person) must be placed by 14:00 (2 pm).
- The minimum order for Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person) is 2.
- Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person) can only be ordered for pickup (takeaway) or a dine-in pre-order with a reservation.
- The kitchen makes a limited number of Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person) each day: 120 portions. Once they are gone, Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person) is sold out until the next day it is served.
- A single regular order can include up to 20 Ramadan Iftar Set Menu (per person).

Choices: Main course — Lamb machboos, Chicken machboos, Harees or Vegetable machboos; Tea — Karak or Sulaimani.

- Eating and drinking in public during fasting hours is permitted in Dubai; the dining room is open from 12:00.

text:

We confirm the exact ready time; collect at the takeaway counter at Gate 3 with your order number. If you are dining in, book a table and add a dine-in pre-order so food is ready when you sit down.

section: Can you guarantee there is absolutely no cross-contamination?
text:
## Can you guarantee there is absolutely no cross-contamination?

Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

- Terrace season: 15 October to 30 April

- Late arrival: table held 15 minutes
- High chairs: 6 in total, up to 4 per booking

section: Personal details Bayt Al Ghaf asks for
text:
## Personal details Bayt Al Ghaf asks for

Bayt Al Ghaf asks for a name and a phone number for every reservation and order, an address for deliveries, and optionally an e-mail address. The phone number is used to confirm the booking, to call about changes, and to identify the guest when they call back.

section: Looking up a Bayt Al Ghaf booking or order
text:
## Looking up a Bayt Al Ghaf booking or order

Staff discuss a reservation or order only with someone who gives its reference (for example RES-482913 or ORD-604215) and the phone number used to make it. After 5 wrong attempts the record is locked for 15 minutes. Details of one guest's booking are never shared with another caller.
